verdicts.misleading_risk: A help.md symptom table is hand-written content that points at anchors in imported guides; the anchors can move when the template or host repos change (check_site catches dead anchors, so a break fails the build, which is a good property). Risk of stating things that are wrong: 'app not in napari/Fiji/QuPath' must link to what the host guide really says; 'build failed' to workflow_status needs the real anchor. The G2 claim that 'SmartScreen' appears only in a screenshot is correct for the built text (my search of site/search.json for 'smartscreen' returned no items). I did not re-run the browser queries; the zero-result outcomes for 'build failed' and 'not showing' and the lack of 'identified developer'/'cannot be opened' in the index are confirmed from the search index text. The empty-panel claim and AND behaviour I did not re-test. An overrides/ no-results message depends on how the Zensical search bundle renders the empty state, which the auditor did not verify.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build the cheapest part first: content/guides/help.md ('Find your problem'), a table of what you see -> link, in the Use track (data/guides.yaml, linked from /use/ via data/hubs.yaml), containing only links to existing anchors, using the exact on-screen strings people see ('Windows protected your PC', 'macOS cannot verify', 'Open Anyway', 'JupyterLab does not start', 'build failed', 'red cross in Actions'). Only list strings verified against the real UI or the guide text. The page text gets indexed, which fixes the synonym problem without touching the search engine. Template repo (LabConstrictor, .tools/docs/install.md): add the literal words 'SmartScreen' and 'unidentified developer' next to the existing step text only if that is what Windows/macOS actually show. Skip the overrides/ empty-state change until someone checks whether the theme supports it; a custom empty state may be fragile on theme update. Add a few query -> expected URL checks as part of G4 (offline against site/search.json).

verdicts.misleading_risk: The literal-Markdown defect is real and confirmed, but its cause is narrower than described. guides.py:23 NAV_BLOCK strips the template's centred footer only when the block contains the capitalised words Previous, Next or Home; template_synchronization.md's footer (template source, line 76-82) uses '← Create repository', '🏠 Documentation home' (lower-case home) and 'Initialise repository →', so it escapes the strip and prints as text. All other guides use Previous/Home/Next and are stripped. So this is one block in one file, not a systemic template problem. A blanket 'give each critical guide the standard skeleton' across 7+ template guides, plus a 'time line', is large editorial work whose numbers (build minutes, token set-up time) the auditor says must be measured; unmeasured text would be invented. The 'before_getting_started' garbled sentence is real: line 27 contains 'pick notebooks. Notebooks have hidden code ... private or public, giving you full control...'. The claim that /build/ puts cards above the 4-step flow was not re-verified by me (hubs.yaml has flow_title: How it works at line 74 but I did not check render order); moving it is a layout change needing a DESIGN.md update and the hub is shared with the Use hub.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Three small, safe edits. (1) Template repo, .tools/docs/template_synchronization.md lines 76-82: change the footer to the standard '[← Previous](create_repository.md) | [🏠 Home](README.md) | [Next →](initialise_repository.md)' so NAV_BLOCK strips it; this also makes the KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS entry in scripts/check_design.py:25 reviewable. Alternatively (site side) make NAV_BLOCK also match the real footer, but the template fix is preferred because it fixes GitHub readers' navigation consistency too. (2) Template repo, .tools/docs/before_getting_started.md line 27: rewrite the garbled paragraph (duplicated sentence, fragment 'private or public, giving you full control...'). (3) Template repo, .tools/docs/create_repository.md and executable_creation.md: add one-line checks only where the real outcome is known (repo shows notebooks/ and .tools/ folders; Actions run is green and the release Assets list the installers), with a link to workflow_status.md / troubleshooting.md. Do not add time estimates until measured. Defer the hub reorder and the other guides until a person has timed the journey; if reordered, update DESIGN.md in the same PR.

verdicts.misleading_risk: The package is too big for a small team: a critical-guides checklist script with heading-regex rules, a spellchecker with allowlist, a search-test corpus, a release checklist and a new workflow step. A heading-pattern check ('check that it worked', 'if it fails') enforces form, not truth: guides could satisfy it with text that is wrong, and it will be red for imported template guides until G3 is done in another repo, forcing a long KNOWN_EXCEPTIONS list that the AGENTS.md 'no silent fallbacks' rule would not like. Item (5) of the 'current' text is partly wrong: GENERIC_LINK_TEXT (check_design.py:21) does not contain 'this guide', so there is no inconsistency; only 'this' and 'this link' are banned. Whether the 'notebook-usage' 'this guide' link points to code-hiding (a Build guide) is a content matter, true as source shows (notebook_usage.md:21). The typos are confirmed in the template source (notebook_usage.md:13 'finnisehd', :21 'LabConstrisctor') but a site-side spellcheck over imported guides would only report problems that must be fixed in other repos. The site-wide daily build opening an issue for foreign content errors may create noise the site team cannot fix.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do only the two cheap, high-value, mechanical checks, in the site repo: (a) in scripts/check_site.py, fail the build when the rendered <main> contains literal Markdown link syntax '](' outside <pre>/<code> (this would have caught the template-synchronization footer today; it is a pure function with a test and a failure case), with the single current offender removed by the template fix in G3 rather than added to an exception list. (b) data/search_tests.yaml (query -> expected URL path prefix) with only queries that work now (the five working ones plus any added by the help page) and a unit test in tests/ that runs them against site/search.json by simple term matching; add the failing ones only after G2's help page lands. Explicitly do not build the 'critical guides' heading checker, the spellchecker or the CI-issue automation yet; keep the human criteria (4 of 5 first-time testers, ~15 min first analysis, per-OS routes) as a short checklist in planning/ naming the owner of each guide, labelled as not automated. Typos should be fixed in the template repo (.tools/docs/notebook_usage.md:13,21 and elsewhere) by a normal PR.
